Just found out the Business Building parking lot is officially closing indefinitely because apparently they discovered the ground underneath is unstable from an old steam tunnel that partially collapsed?? 😐 So you’re telling me the ONE lot that’s actually close to class is gone because K-State built it on top of a 1950s utility tunnel that’s now sinking?? And they’re not creating temporary parking?? Love that for us. 😒 Guess I’ll just plan to park across campus and hike to my class. Tuition goes up but parking spots go down. Make it make sense.

Okay but north side of campus is finally getting some love!! Just saw the announcement that K-State is building a new parking lot by Thockmorton Hall, and honestly… it’s about time. They’re adding over 400 new spots. Building is set to be finished by summer of next year. Apparently it’s part of a push to ease congestion on the north side since enrollment in engineering and ag programs keeps growing. No more circling the lot 3 times before an 8:30. If this actually means I don’t have to risk parking in Administration spots and praying I don’t come back to a $30-$50 ticket on my windshield, I’m calling it a win.

Lowkey tired of seeing everyone my age “winning” already. Every time I open an app, someone’s launching a startup, getting shredded, traveling the world, or posting their six-figure job offer. Meanwhile I’m just trying to pass my classes and remember to do laundry. Feels like if you’re not constantly improving, optimizing, grinding, you’re falling behind. No breaks. No excuses. Sometimes it feels like average just isn’t allowed anymore.

Lowkey trying to remind myself that everyone’s path looks different—and that’s okay. Every time I open an app, I see people launching startups, getting in shape, traveling, or landing big job offers—and it’s honestly inspiring. Meanwhile, I’m focusing on passing my classes, building my own routine, and yes, remembering to do laundry. It might not look flashy, but it’s still progress. Growth doesn’t have to be constant or extreme to count. I’m learning that taking things at my own pace, giving myself breaks, and showing up consistently is enough. “Average” isn’t failure—it’s just part of the process. And there’s still so much time to figure things out.
